Gladinet CentreStack and TrioFox contain a hardcoded cryptographic keys vulnerability for their implementation of the AES cryptoscheme. This vulnerability degrades security for public exposed endpoints that may make use of it and may offer arbitrary local file inclusion when provided a specially crafted request without authentication.

WatchGuard Fireware OS iked process contains an out of bounds write vulnerability in the OS iked process. This vulnerability may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code and affects both the mobile user VPN with IKEv2 and the branch office VPN using IKEv2 when configured with a dynamic gateway peer.

Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security (ASA) Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software VPN Web Server contain a buffer overflow vulnerability that allows for remote code execution. This vulnerability could be chained with CVE-2025-20362.

Cisco IOS and IOS XE contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem that could allow for denial of service or remote code execution. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system.

Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security (ASA) Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software VPN Web Server contain a missing authorization vulnerability. This vulnerability could be chained with CVE-2025-20333.
Samsung mobile devices contain an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libimagecodec.quram.so. This vulnerability could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.
Samsung mobile devices contain an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libimagecodec.quram.so which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.
Microsoft Windows Hyper-V NT Kernel Integration VSP contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows a local attacker to gain SYSTEM privileges.

Microsoft Windows Storage contains a link following vulnerability that could allow for privilege escalation. This vulnerability could allow an attacker to delete data including data that results in the service being unavailable.
Juniper Junos OS contains an improper isolation or compartmentalization vulnerability. This vulnerability could allows a local attacker with high privileges to inject arbitrary code.

VMware ESXi contains an arbitrary write vulnerability. Successful exploitation allows an attacker with privileges within the VMX process to trigger an arbitrary kernel write leading to an escape of the sandbox.
Ivanti Connect Secure, Policy Secure, and ZTA Gateways contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution.

SonicWall SMA1000 Appliance Management Console (AMC) and Central Management Console (CMC) contain a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability, which can enable a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands.
Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy contain an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows a remote attacker to gain super-admin privileges via crafted CSF proxy requests.
Microsoft Windows New Technology File System (NTFS) contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.
Fortinet FortiOS, FortiSwitchManager, and FortiSASE contain a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows an attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via specially crafted packets.
SolarWinds Web Help Desk contain a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in AjaxProxy that could allow an attacker to run commands on the host machine.
Microsoft Windows Management Console (MMC) contains an improper neutralization vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.

tj-actions/changed-files GitHub Action contains an embedded malicious code vulnerability that allows a remote attacker to discover secrets by reading Github Actions Workflow Logs. These secrets may include, but are not limited to, valid AWS access keys, GitHub personal access tokens (PATs), npm tokens, and private RSA keys.

Apple Safari, iOS, watchOS, visionOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS contain a buffer overflow vulnerability that could allow the processing of maliciously crafted web content which may lead to memory corruption.
SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer Metadata Uploader contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated agent to upload potentially malicious executable binaries.
Craft CMS contains a code injection vulnerability that allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code.
Langflow contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v1/validate/code endpoint that allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code via crafted HTTP requests.

Langflow contains an origin validation error vulnerability in which an overly permissive CORS configuration combined with a refresh token cookie configured as SameSite=None allows a malicious webpage to perform cross-origin requests that include credentials and successfully call the refresh endpoint. This could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and achieve full system compromise via obtained tokens that permit access to authenticated endpoints.
Linux kernel contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that has a high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
Commvault Web Server contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows a remote, authenticated attacker to create and execute webshells.

Linux Kernel contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive path which allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass the intended recvmsg() record-type handling, potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Linux Kernel contains a race condition vulnerability which allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket causing data to be unpredictably interleaved and creating inconsistencies in the socket's internal state.

Broadcom VMware Aria Operations and VMware Tools contain a privilege defined with unsafe actions vulnerability. A malicious local actor with non-administrative privileges having access to a VM with VMware Tools installed and managed by Aria Operations with SDMP enabled may exploit this vulnerability to escalate privileges to root on the same VM.

Qualitia Active! Mail contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary or trigger a denial-of-service via a specially crafted request.
Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS, contain an unspecified vulnerability when processing a maliciously crafted photo or video shared via an iCloud Link.

Apple watchOS, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS, and tvOS contain an improper locking vulnerability that could allow a malicious application to cause unexpected changes in memory shared between processes.

Apple watchOS, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS, and tvOS contain a classic buffer overflow vulnerability which could allow a malicious application to cause unexpected system termination or write kernel memory.

Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and other Apple products contain a use-after-free vulnerability in WebKit. Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to memory corruption. Git contains a link following vulnerability that stems from Git’s inconsistent handling of carriage return characters in configuration files.
Android Framework contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for privilege escalation.
Android Framework contains an integer overflow vulnerability that allows for code execution that could allow for local privilege escalation.
Android Framework contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for information disclosure.

F5 BIG-IP APM contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that could allow a threat actor to achieve remote code execution.

This vulnerability could be chained with CVE-2025-53771. Meta React Server Components contains a remote code execution vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution by exploiting a flaw in how React decodes payloads sent to React Server Function endpoints. Please note CVE-2025-66478 has been rejected, but it is associated with CVE-2025- 55182.

Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability due to insufficient input validation. This vulnerability can lead to memory overread when the NetScaler is configured as a Gateway (VPN virtual server, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) OR AAA virtual server.

Sangoma FreePBX contains an authentication bypass vulnerability due to insufficiently sanitized user-supplied data allows unauthenticated access to FreePBX Administrator leading to arbitrary database manipulation and remote code execution.

Fortinet FortiWeb contains an OS command Injection vulnerability that may allow an authenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code on the underlying system via crafted HTTP requests or CLI commands.

OSGeo GeoServer contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that occurs when the application accepts XML input through a specific endpoint /geoserver/wms operation GetMap and could allow an attacker to define external entities within the XML request.

ASUS Live Update contains an embedded malicious code vulnerability client were distributed with unauthorized modifications introduced through a supply chain compromise. Users should discontinue product utilization.
Microsoft Windows contains a link following vulnerability that allows for privilege escalation

FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager contain a path traversal vulnerability that may allow an authenticated attacker with admin profile and at least read-write permissions to write or delete arbitrary files via specific CLI commands.
Oracle Fusion Middleware contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to take over Identity Manager.

Oracle E-Business Suite contains an unspecified vulnerability in the BI Publisher Integration component. Oracle E-Business Suite contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in the Runtime component of Oracle Configurator. This vulnerability is remotely exploitable without authentication.

Motex LANSCOPE Endpoint Manager contains an improper verification of source of a communication channel vulnerability allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending specially crafted packets.
Microsoft Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver contains a use after free vulnerability that can allow an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

Ray-Project Ray contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow remote code execution. Developers using Ray as a development tool may be exposed to this vulnerability exploitable through Firefox and Safari.
Fortinet FortiWeb contains a relative path traversal vulnerability that may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute administrative commands on the system via crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests.

Google Chromium contains an improper input validation vulnerability in ANGLE and GPU. This vulnerability could allow a remote attacker to potentially perform a sandbox escape via a crafted HTML page. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.
Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Classic UI where attackers could abuse Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) @import directives in email HTML.
Lantronix EDS5000 contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow attackers to inject arbitrary OS commands into the username parameter. Injected commands are executed with root privileges.
n8n contains an improper control of dynamically managed code resources vulnerability in its workflow expression evaluation system that allows for remote code execution.

Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) contains a PHP remote file inclusion vulnerability that could allow for remote attackers to craft requests to the /h/rest endpoint to influence internal request dispatching, allowing inclusion of arbitrary files from the WebRoot directory.

Fortinet FortiOS contains an exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor vulnerability. This may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests. An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.
Gogs contains a path traversal vulnerability affecting improper Symbolic link handling in the PutContents API that could allow for code execution.
N-able N-Central contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that could lead to command execution.

TP-Link Archer C7(EU) and TL-WR841N/ND(MS) contain an OS command injection vulnerability that exists in the Parental Control page. The impacted products could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users should discontinue product utilization.
Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorized VPN connection.

Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall.
Langflow contains an inclusion of functionality from untrusted control sphere vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations.

Zammad GmbH Zammad contains an improper privilege management vulnerability that can allow the local zammad user to escalate privileges to root. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-102489.
BeyondTrust Remote Support contains an authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to perform file operations on the appliance.

GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml.

Fortinet FortiMail contains a path traversal and an improper neutralization of NULL byte or NULL character vulnerability that may allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying system via crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests.
Ivanti Connect Secure contains an authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands.

Ahsay AhsayCBS contains an improper authentication vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to bypass authentication via manipulation of the random parameter in the API component’s checkSysPwd function. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-105134.

Ahsay AhsayCBS contains a command injection vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute operating system commands via manipulation of the random parameter in the Replication Receiver component’s /rps/api/json/UpdateReceivers.do endpoint. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-105133.

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. PHP contains an out-of-memory corruption vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
PHP contains a stale internal request-state vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.

Collabora Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server when used within the NextCloud platform contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows for remote code execution when the CODE server isn't running.

Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.

Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.

Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG), Load Balancer, Application Delivery Controller (ADC), Message Archiver (BMA), WAF Control Center (WCC), Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Web Security Gateway (WSG) contain an OS command injection vulnerability. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-116606

Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder contains an incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability that may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience.

Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator on-prem contains a SQL injection vulnerability that may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.

Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-111560.
SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability that permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution.

Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357.

WordPress WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window. This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades.

Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.
OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux contains an unexpected status code or return value vulnerability that could allow for authentication bypass.
IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations.
PTC Windchill and FlexPLM contains an improper input validation vulnerability allowing an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending a malicious request to the network.

SonicWall SMA1000 Appliances contain a server-side request forgery vulnerability that could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to potentially cause the appliance to make requests to unintended location.

SonicWall SMA1000 Appliances contain a code injection vulnerability which in specific conditions could potentially enable a remote authenticated attacker as administrator to execute arbitrary OS commands.

Check Point SmartConsole contains an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token and use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.

Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem contains an OS command injection vulnerability that may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and data managed by the orchestrator.
N-able N-central contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that allows for authentication bypass.

N-able N-central contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel allows for authentication bypass and account takeover in N-central. This vulnerability is the result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556.

Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway contain an authentication-bypass vulnerability involving an alternate path or channel. SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN contains a use of single-factor authentication vulnerability that may allow a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls. Successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Software and Cisco Security Cloud Control (SCC) Firewall Management contain an authentication Bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and execute script files on an affected device to obtain root access to the underlying operating system.

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller & Manager contain an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system.

Cisco Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM) and Cisco Unified Communications Manager Session Management Edition (Unified CM SME) contain a server-side request forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.

Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) formerly known as Firepower Management Center contains a use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account to access sensitive data within the impacted systems.

Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.

Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) contain a heap inspection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.
Microsoft Windows Desktop Windows Manager contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

Multiple Atlassian products (Bitbucket Data Center ,Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye) contain a files or directories accessible to external parties vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions.

Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in contain an improper access control vulnerability that can result in unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data as well as unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in accessible data.

SmarterTools SmarterMail contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the password reset API. The force-reset-password endpoint permits anonymous requests and fails to verify the existing password or a reset token when resetting system administrator accounts. This could allow an unauthenticated attacker to supply a target administrator username and a new password to reset the account, resulting in full administrative compromise of the SmarterMail instance.
GNU InetUtils contains an argument injection vulnerability in telnetd that could allow for remote authentication bypass via a "-f root" value for the USER environment variable.

SmarterTools SmarterMail contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in the ConnectToHub API method. This could allow the attacker to point the SmarterMail instance to a malicious HTTP server which serves the malicious OS command and could lead to command execution.

SolarWinds Serv-U contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header to crash the Serv-U service without authentication.
Linux Kernel contains an incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability that could allow for privilege escalation.
Microsoft SharePoint Server contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

Microsoft Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions contains a double free vulnerability that could enable remote code execution.
Apache ActiveMQ contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows for code injection.

BerriAI LiteLLM contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows an attacker to read data from the proxy's database and potentially modify it, leading to unauthorized access to the proxy and the credentials it manages.
BerriAI LiteLLM contains a command injection vulnerability that could allow any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands on the host.

TanStack contains an unspecified vulnerability that allowed malicious versions of the product to be published to the npm registry to publish credential-stealing malware under a trusted identity.

Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows a remotely authenticated user with administrative access to achieve remote code execution.

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2025-02-13.

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-11-15.

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, CivetWeb permits unauthenticated clients to flood the WebUI login page and API invalid paths without connection or request-rate limits. Repeated requests can consume substantial CPU in request processing and session authentication, making the WebUI sluggish or unresponsive and potentially affecting the wider system and DNS service. Requests to selected invalid or redirecting paths also generate a log entry for each request, allowing network traffic to expand logs and exhaust constrained storage such as an SD card, while other request forms consume CPU without producing a corresponding request log. The Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.0.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit succeeds even though wp_kses is applied on save, because the XSS is manufactured post-sanitization by the plugin's regex pass: kses-permitted tags such as <a title> and <code> carry the attacker's marker and terminator strings intact into the rendered HTML buffer, where the plugin's own replacement then corrupts the document structure.

An unauthenticated attacker can request /auth/ssh_challenge_token for an arbitrary account by supplying X-Rucio-Account, then present the returned X-Rucio-SSH-Challenge-Token as X-Rucio-Auth-Token to authenticate to other API endpoints as that account, including an administrative account. This issue is fixed in versions 35.9.1, 38.6.1, 40.4.2, and 41.1.1.

HtmlSanitizer is a .NET library for cleaning HTML fragments and documents from constructs that can lead to XSS attacks. Prior to 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta, HtmlSanitizer CSS style-declaration sanitization can process an attacker-controlled style attribute with quadratic cost because SanitizeStyleDeclaration repeatedly causes the complete declaration to be serialized while removing disallowed CSS properties. One unauthenticated request can occupy a synchronous application worker for seconds, and concurrent requests can saturate all workers and sustain denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta.

Instatic is an open source visual content management system for building static websites. Prior to 0.0.14, isSafeUrl() and safeUrl() in src/core/html-sanitize/index.ts remove tabs, newlines, carriage returns, and characters handled by String.prototype.trim(), but leave other leading C0 control characters that browsers discard before parsing a URL scheme. A low-privileged editor can place a dangerous URL behind one of those controls in a URL property or custom HTML attribute, allowing src/core/publisher/escapeProps.ts and the shared URL sanitizer to emit it into rendered content. When an Owner or Admin activates the element in the same-origin admin editor canvas, script executes with the victim's application authority and can drive admin APIs to read protected data, create an owner account, or install a plugin. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.14.

Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.

The Envira Gallery  WordPress plugin before 1.16.4 does not apply its own gallery-permission policy until an administrator first opens its permissions screen, instead copying gallery-management capabilities onto each role from that role's core post capabilities after activation, which lets Contributor accounts create, edit and delete galleries that the policy is meant to restrict to higher roles.

Chevereto before 4.5.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to cause the server to issue arbitrary requests by supplying a malicious URL to the uploadToWebsite function, which fetches the raw source via fetch_url before the Upload::checkValidUrl SSRF guard can be invoked. Attackers can target loopback addresses, RFC1918 internal services, cloud instance metadata endpoints, and file/gopher/dict schemes through the /json upload action to disclose internal responses or credentials when the fetched content is stored and served back as a public image URL.

A maliciously crafted DWG file, when parsed by Autodesk AutoCAD, can trigger an Integer Overflow vulnerability in RLE bitmap decompression, resulting in an undersized heap allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

The Delivery & Pickup Date Time for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.3.90. This is due to a nonce-only settings AJAX handler that stores an attribute-breaking value and an administrator settings template that outputs it without HTML attribute escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

A path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) was found in ansible-core's ansible-galaxy role installation. An explicit role "name" taken from a role's meta/requirements.yml is used to construct the on-disk installation path without validating that the resulting destination stays within the selected roles directory. A name containing "../" escapes that directory, and an absolute name replaces it entirely. Because ansible-galaxy processes transitive dependencies from an installed role's meta/requirements.yml, a malicious role publisher can cause attacker-supplied files to be written outside the operator's chosen roles directory when the operator installs the role, and, when --force is used, can cause an existing role directory outside that path to be removed and replaced. The impact is bounded by the invoking user's filesystem permissions and requires the operator to install the attacker-influenced content.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('OS command injection') vulnerability in Westell Technologies, Inc Remote series products on Linux allows OS Command Injection.

This issue affects several generations of Westell Remotes: through firmware version 9.14.  It has been reproduced across multiple devices. However, it is confirmed to affect only devices configured for RAS (Remote Access Server - e.g., RADIUS, TACACS).

A flaw was found in CRI-O. When the optional Linux LinkLogs feature is enabled, the host pod log directory is bind-mounted into a pod emptyDir and is intended to be read-only, but Linux ignores MS_RDONLY on the initial bind and the CRI mount stays writable. A non-privileged UID 0 container can place a symlink at a future kubelet log path so that privileged conmon later appends attacker-controlled log data to an existing host file. This is an append-only host integrity issue, not universal remote code execution; LinkLogs is not enabled by default.

EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition contains an OS command injection vulnerability which may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands with root or SYSTEM privileges on the system running the affected product.

The Royal Addons for Elementor  WordPress plugin before 1.7.1071 does not restrict or validate the post meta keys used when counting or rendering a filtered grid, and does not reject private (hidden) meta keys, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the value of arbitrary private post meta one value at a time from the filtered result count. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-17585, whose 1.7.1067 patch covered only a separate search-based path and left the grid filtering path affected.

The Bizuno Accounting – ERP/Accounting/CRM (for WordPress) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Password Reset Token Disclosure in all versions up to, and including, 7.4.5 via the `bizUser` parameter of the `validateReset()` function on the `portal/api/lostPW` endpoint. This is due to `portalCtl::goAPI()` failing to call `loadBusinessCache()` before invoking the handler, which causes `isMailConfigured()` to read an empty business cache and return false regardless of the site's actual mail configuration, causing the fully-qualified reset URL — containing the victim's live reset UUID and numeric user ID — to be embedded directly in the HTML response rather than delivered by email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain a valid password-reset token for any Bizuno account, including administrators, directly from the HTTP response and submit it to the `portal/api/lostVal` endpoint to rewrite the victim's password and achieve full account takeover. The administrator email address required to initiate the reset is frequently exposed by the plugin's own login error messages and the public `/bizuno/` portal page, making exploitation trivial against most installations.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not correctly restrict which database tables an administrator of a single site may operate on in a multisite network, allowing subsite administrators to read and modify the tables of other sites and of the network, and to make themselves Super Admin.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not restrict one of its database tools to network administrators on multisite installations, allowing administrators of a single subsite to run arbitrary SQL against the whole network's database and make themselves Super Admin.

tiny-secp256k1 is a tiny secp256k1 native/JS wrapper. From 2.1.0 until 2.2.5 for tiny-secp256k1 and from 2.2.2 until 2.2.5 for @bitcoin-js/tiny-secp256k1-asmjs, the three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the backend failure return from xOnlyPointAddTweak when a tweak produces the point at infinity. The shared X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT buffer then still contains the original point, so a caller-controlled resultToCheck equal to that point can make the stale-buffer comparison return true even though no tweaked key exists. Protocols that rely on this helper to validate caller-controlled internal keys, tweaks, and comparison values can accept an invalid derived key. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.5.

The SAML SSO Login  WordPress plugin through 1.5.2 does not verify that the SAML assertion whose signature it validates is the same assertion it reads the user identity from, allowing unauthenticated attackers who hold a validly signed assertion for any identity to authenticate as any existing user, including an administrator, through XML signature wrapping.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to second-order SQL Injection via the user profile description field in all Free versions up to, and including, 1.26.15 and all Premium versions up to, and including, 2.26.15. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to store a malicious payload that is written into a database backup and executed as SQL when an administrator later restores that backup. Successful exploitation can modify sensitive WordPress data and, on sites where plugin installation is available, lead to remote code execution through the installation and activation of an attacker-controlled plugin.

The WP Maps – Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, Mapbox, Store Locator with Search, Filters & Listings plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'csv_columns' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

OmniFaces is a utility library for Faces. From 5.2 until 5.4.3, applications using <o:sse> or @Push(type=SSE) with session scope, view scope, or a user attribute can expose pushed messages because org.omnifaces.cdi.push.SseEndpoint#doGet accepts a channel identifier registered by SseChannelManager and PushSessionManager without verifying that the caller's HTTP session owns it. An attacker who obtains the victim's channel identifier from a logged URL, report, Referer header, or shared link can connect from a foreign or absent session and receive messages intended for the victim. Application-scoped channels are intentionally unbound, and this issue permits message receipt but not message injection. This issue is fixed in version 5.4.3.

The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

CAST Imaging is vulnerable to authentication bypass in the TenantFilter class. The TenantFilter processes the X-ISSUER-LOCATION HTTP header and dynamically registers an OpenID Connect issuer based on its value. An unauthenticated remote attacker can register a malicious identity provider, create users matching existing administrative usernames, and obtain valid JWTs which will be accepted by the application. This results in complete authentication bypass and privilege escalation to administrative access.




The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging has multiple path traversal vulnerabilities in various endpoints. The application does not properly validate the path parameters, allowing an authenticated attacker to use "../" sequences to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.


Critically, by reading "/proc/self/environ", the attacker can obtain environment variables containing sensitive credentials such as Keycloak and PostgreSQL passwords, leading to full server compromise and administrative access.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging has a missing authentication vulnerability in the "/api/auth/keycloak/users/{username}" endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker can modify the email address of an arbitrary Keycloak user and access sensitive account information, including the API authentication token hash. This can lead to account takeover, user impersonation and user enumeration.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging is vulnerable to Path Traversal vulnerability in "/api/server-folders" and "/api/server-folders/download" endpoints. These file-management endpoints accept user-supplied filesystem paths and allow selected system commands to be executed at the specified location, but they do not enforce sufficient authorization boundaries or restrict access to a predefined set of resources. An authenticated attacker can enumerate server directories via the "ls" command and retrieve arbitrary files outside of the intended application workspace, such as "/etc/passwd", exposing sensitive data.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging contains a hardcoded authentication token in the "KeyCloakController" class of auth-service.jar. An attacker who gains access to the source code, application package, logs, or configuration files can reuse this token to call auth-service endpoints without authentication. Using the token with the "/api/auth/keycloak/users" endpoint, the attacker can enumerate users across Keycloak realms and retrieve user attributes containing API token hashes, enabling reconnaissance and further exploitation.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging does not properly check whether a user is authorized to modify another user's notification settings in the "/api/admin/user/update-subscriber" endpoint. An authenticated, low-privileged attacker can enable or disable email notifications on another user's behalf, which can suppress important communications such as security alerts and disrupt business processes.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging allows authenticated, low-privileged users to access parts of the administrator panel. When a user navigates to any URL path the application doesn't recognize, a wildcard route automatically redirects them to the administrative view at "/admin/applications". This allows an attacker to perform certain administrator-restricted actions, including triggering app-to-app link generation, configuring regexes, and changing searchable object properties, resulting in unauthorized modification of application configuration.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging has an access control flaw in the "/api/jobs/<uuid>/logs/download" endpoint. An authenticated low-privilege user can download log archives for any job whose UUID they know, even if they are not authorized to access it.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

The Unzer Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1. The vulnerability exists because the Google Pay Express Checkout endpoint (`/?wc-api=google_pay_express`), handled by `startCheckoutDataWithNormalizedCustomerData`, accepts an attacker-controlled `paymentData.email` value and passes it to `createOrGetGuestCustomer()`, which resolves the submitted email to any existing WordPress user via `get_user_by('email', ...)` and then calls `wp_set_current_user()` and `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for the resolved user ID without verifying ownership of the email address, a password, a nonce, an authentication token, or any proof of payment from the payment provider. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress user — including administrators — by submitting that user's known email address, receiving valid `wordpress_logged_in_*` session cookies for the targeted account and achieving full site takeover. The endpoint is entirely unprotected with no capability check, nonce validation, or payment-provider signature verification applied, and administrator email addresses are frequently discoverable via the WordPress REST API user enumeration endpoint (`/wp-json/wp/v2/users`), author archive pages, Gravatar lookups, or site contact footers.

An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user ID matched an enterprise's numeric ID to manage that enterprise's GitHub Apps and generate private keys without enterprise membership. GitHub App ownership checks compared numeric IDs without checking the owner's account type. Exploitation required control of a session for the colliding user account and an enterprise-owned GitHub App. A generated private key could be used to authenticate as the App and access repositories where it was installed, within its granted permissions. On standard fresh installations, the documented collision involved the non-loginable built-in ghost account; the reported GHES reproduction used site administrator impersonation. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

The Comelit 1456B Multi-User Gateway, in firmware versions up to and including 2.10.0, is configured with static default passwords for multiple privileged roles. None of these passwords are required to be changed during initial configuration, and they remain at their default values unless the administrator changes them manually. An attacker with network access to the device can authenticate using these default credentials and gain administrative control.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

The AIKTP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Predictable Token in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.7. The vulnerability exists because the plugin's sync token (`aiktpz_token`) is generated using PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid()` function — producing a wall-clock-derived value with approximately one million microsecond candidates per uncertain generation second — while the unauthenticated, unthrottled REST endpoint `/wp-json/aiktp/checkToken` (registered with `permission_callback => __return_true`) acts as a public brute-force oracle for the token; simultaneously, the capability checks in `check_valid_token` and its wrappers (`verify_aiktp_token_with_edit_capability`, `verify_aiktp_token_with_upload_capability`) inspect only a server-side stored Administrator account (option `aiktp_author`) rather than the actual REST caller, meaning possession of the token alone grants Administrator-equivalent authority to any external request. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover the sync token and then invoke `POST /wp-json/aiktp/createpost` to publish arbitrary posts attributed to a site Administrator, `POST /wp-json/aiktp/doUpdatePostWithImageURL` to overwrite the body content of any existing post, and `POST /wp-json/aiktp/doUploadImageToWP` to import remote media and attach it as the featured image of any post. Additionally, when the `aiktpz_token` option has never been initialized, the `checkToken` oracle returns success for an empty token submission due to a loose comparison in `check_valid_token`, providing a zero-effort bypass that requires no brute-forcing whatsoever.

The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.

libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 5.1.22, the @libp2p/crypto code reached by the default Identify service accepts a remote peer’s crafted publicKey before peer-id or signature verification and passes it through publicKeyFromProtobuf to the ASN.1 DER decoder. readLength in packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts accepts long-form element lengths larger than the remaining buffer, causing readInteger and related readers to loop synchronously over an attacker-claimed length from a very small key blob. Because decoding occurs in one event-loop tick before the remotePeer equality check in packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts, the Identify timeout cannot interrupt it, allowing repeated unauthenticated connections to stall all timers and peers and transiently exhaust memory. This issue is fixed in version 5.1.22.

The Trust Payments Gateway for WooCommerce (JavaScript Library) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.8. The vulnerability exists because the `new_customer_account()` function stores the raw return value of `wp_create_user()` — including a `WP_Error` object returned on username collision — into the order's `tp_userid` post meta before the `is_wp_error()` guard is evaluated; the `add_customer_details_to_thankyou_page()` callback subsequently reads that meta and casts it with `(int)`, causing PHP to coerce any object to integer `1`, after which `wp_set_current_user(1)` and `wp_set_auth_cookie(1)` are called unconditionally. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as WordPress user ID 1 — the bootstrap site administrator or, on multisite, a network super-admin — by supplying the `new_username` parameter matching any existing login during checkout and visiting the resulting thank-you page. Exploitation requires the Trust Payments gateway to be active and the attacker to complete a paid order on their own account; the ID 1 administrator username is additionally enumerable via standard WordPress user enumeration techniques.

The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content/excerpt (REST wp/v2/posts) → stored in post_content/post_excerpt' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor's entity-encoded payload survives save-time wp_kses filtering verbatim and is only decoded into raw script tags at render time via html_entity_decode(), meaning the injected script executes for every visitor — including authenticated Administrators — once an Editor publishes the post through the standard Contributor workflow.

An authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed authenticated users to read review-thread data from private repositories they could not access. An attacker required an authenticated account, a readable repository and pull request to use as the request context, and target review-thread identifiers. The thread-preview endpoint resolved supplied identifiers without restricting them to the authorized pull request, exposing private file paths and, when positioning and diff data were available, source-code excerpts, commit identifiers, and line metadata without victim interaction. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases in the 3.21, 3.22 series and was fixed in versions 3.21.10, 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. When processing a specially crafted JPEG 2000 image, data read from adjacent dynamic memory may be incorporated into the pixels of the decoded image and result in information disclosure to anyone who can access the output.

Vulnerability involving the exposure of sensitive information in the URLs of the UOC Virtual Campus’s document upload feature. This data may be stored in the browser history and in server or proxy logs, or transmitted via the HTTP Referer header, depending on the configuration and browsing flow. Its inclusion in the URL could allow for the unauthorized disclosure of information to third parties with access to those logs or recipients.

A command injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated site administrator to execute arbitrary commands as the host git user on peer Git server nodes outside the pre-receive hook sandbox by supplying a crafted pre-receive environment download URL. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, 3.20.12, and 3.19.16. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IoT) Development Framework. Prior to 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3, the Bluedroid BLE Mesh GATT server read handler bt_mesh_bta_gatts_cb in esp_ble_mesh stores a signed attribute-read callback length in an unsigned 16-bit variable. A negative ATT error code is therefore interpreted as a very large successful length and used for a memory copy from a small stack buffer into the GATT response structure. A remote attacker within Bluetooth LE range who can connect to an exposed PB-GATT provisioning or Mesh Proxy service can trigger a failed attribute read with a crafted request. On devices where the affected attributes are accessible without pairing, exploitation requires neither pairing nor user interaction; access requirements depend on device configuration. The resulting out-of-bounds read and stack-based buffer overflow corrupts the Bluetooth host task stack, causing a crash and device restart and potentially further memory corruption. The issue affects devices built with CONFIG_BT_BLUEDROID_ENABLED=y and BLE Mesh GATT enabled; the NimBLE host path is not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3.

Doorkeeper is an OAuth 2 provider for Ruby on Rails / Grape. Prior to 5.9.1, Doorkeeper's OAuth token revocation flow does not correctly authorize revocation requests when public, non-confidential clients are used, allowing tokens to be revoked without correct authorization. This issue is fixed in version 5.9.1.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When a task or its parameters are marked no_log: true, sensitive values passed to a module's warn() or deprecate() calls are not redacted and are printed in cleartext to stdout/stderr in warning and deprecation messages. The 'warnings' and 'deprecations' keys are retained in the PRESERVE allow-list in lib/ansible/_internal/_task.py when the task result is censored, so sensitive parameters bypass masking and can be disclosed in output captured in terminal sessions, CI logs, and any automation wrapping ansible-playbook, even though every task touching the secrets is marked no_log: true.

In specific versions of Octopus Tentacle, Tentacle fails to unset registration credentials as environment variables, resulting in deployment scripts potentially having the ability to read those credentials.

The Kirki – Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (title attribute of <abbr>)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to run the Kirki Convert (migration) workflow on a page containing the attacker's approved comment, as the browser-side DOM parser decodes the kses-allowed abbr title attribute value into a raw XSS payload that is then persisted without sanitization and later rendered unescaped. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The rus to lat advanced plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 via the '_cf7mls_db_form_data_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete arbitrary stored Contact Form 7 submissions from the database. Exploitation requires the companion CF7 Database plugin to be active and the per-form "Save every step, not just the final submission" option to be enabled.

The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to missing authorization to Unauthorized Social App Data Modification in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 This is due to missing authentication, nonce, and capability checks in the `standardFSApp()` function, which is registered on the `wp` action hook and executes on every frontend page load without any login or permission verification. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to insert arbitrary social network app records into the database, or overwrite the OAuth `client_id` and `client_secret` of existing social network connections, by supplying attacker-controlled values via the `fsp_app_redirect` and `app` GET parameters. An attacker can target a specific existing social app record for credential overwrite by supplying matching `social_network` and `slug` values, requiring no knowledge of internal record IDs, which disrupts scheduled social media posts and forces administrators to re-authenticate their connected accounts.

This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.

The Geo Mashup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (comment form) / display_name (profile form)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.13.23 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The comment-author path requires the crafted comment to be approved before the payload is served to visitors; the subscriber-level path requires the plugin's user-location mapping feature to be enabled.

The Check & Log Email – Easy Email Testing & Mail logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires an administrator to approve the comment carrying the shortcode payload, and the target page must render the core Latest Comments block, which passes comment author names through do_shortcode via the_content.

The Custom Twitter Feeds – A Tweets Widget or X Feed Widget plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'atts (JSON object, specifically the inner `feed` key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is first stored in the wp_ctf_feed_caches database table and later written into the ctf_cron_report WordPress option by the scheduled ctf_feed_update cron job, meaning execution is deferred until the cron runs and an administrator subsequently loads the Support page.

The Jeg Kit for Elementor – Powerful Addons for Elementor, Widgets & Templates for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution requires a published page containing both a Post Author widget in user_bio mode (rendering the attacker's biography) and any legitimate jkit_client_logo widget, so that client-logo.js is enqueued and the loadCarousel handler fires against the forged widget markup from the bio field.

A site administrator could modify files on the appliance host with root privileges and disclose private repository data due to improper path validation in GitHub Enterprise Server. Exploitation required a crafted pre-receive hook environment. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server versions prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

An SSH certificate authentication bypass vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed an authenticated organization member to read and modify another user's private repositories within the trusted certificate authority's scope. Exploitation required an instance using built-in authentication and a valid certificate issued to the attacker by a trusted SSH certificate authority. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

The Advanced Country Blocker plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script is stored via the advcb_live_activity transient on the init hook and executed when an administrator views the Live Monitor page, as the stored URI is unsafely concatenated into a double-quoted HTML title attribute and inserted into the DOM via jQuery .html().

The The GDPR Framework By Data443 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.2. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete all postmeta rows for every Easy Digital Downloads payment order on the site, destroying order metadata belonging to all customers. Exploitation requires that Easy Digital Downloads 2.x is active and the GDPR Framework's EDD compatibility option is enabled with a delete or delete_and_notify action configured.

Description:

When an iRule that processes client traffic using the GENERICMESSAGE::route command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). 





Impact:



Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.







Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to authenticated users, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to disclose the name and content of non-public templates stored on the site.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not verify that the acting user is authorised to modify the target post when saving a template, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to overwrite the content and type of an arbitrary post, including another user's published page, removing it from the front end.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not sanitise post meta saved through an AJAX action, nor escape it when rendering the product page, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor (who lack the unfiltered_html capability) to store JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who views the product, including administrators.

The Dynific Addons for Elementor (formerly Anywhere Elementor) WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not perform a capability check on an AJAX action that stores a configuration value, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to store a value that is later output without proper escaping in a quoted attribute on an administrator settings page, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the administrator's session.

Typecho before 1.3.1-rc contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the XML-RPC pingback.ping method where checkSafeHost() validates a hostname's resolved IP once but the subsequent outbound request performs an independent DNS resolution, creating a TOCTOU window exploitable via DNS rebinding. An unauthenticated attacker can configure a domain to return a benign IP at validation time and an internal address (loopback, RFC1918, or cloud metadata IP) at request time, causing the server to issue blind SSRF requests to arbitrary internal hosts and ports.

Pleasanter contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Publishing feature. If this vulnerability is exploited, a remote unauthenticated attacker who can access a site published using the product may obtain, by sending a specially crafted request, information on records of unpublished sites (e.g., titles), as well as the names of users, groups, and organizations registered in the same tenant. Note that the vulnerability only affects configurations where both of the following conditions are met: a site is published using the Publishing feature, and the published site contains link items (items linked to other sites, users, groups, or organizations).

A Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information (CWE-319) vulnerability exists in the Android application "Imperial Palaces Guide" provided by The Imperial Household Agency. A man-in-the-middle attacker may be able to tamper with data transmitted between the application and the server, resulting in the display of modified content to users.

Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode.

Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input.

This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0.

The JobBoardWP – Job Board Listings and Submissions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'job_description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin's default public submission workflow auto-provisions a jb_employer account for any visitor, meaning the effective entry point is unauthenticated — the custom role requirement imposes no real barrier on a stock install.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

The DataPress (Dataverse Integration) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.97 via the 'src' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Exploitation requires WP_DEBUG to be defined as true on the target site — not the default on production, but commonly enabled on staging, development, and misconfigured production environments.

The Toolbox for Asgaros Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_temp_pics function in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.4. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). This vulnerability is only reachable when the site administrator has enabled the Inline Image Upload feature (disabled by default).

The HTML Forms – Simple WordPress Forms Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'arbitrary POST parameter NAME (the array key, not the value)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping.
