The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.

The AI Puffer - MCP Server for Claude & ChatGPT, with AI Chatbot plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via AI-generated comment replies in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.28 due to insufficient sanitization of the AI model's output in the insert_comment_reply_logic() function, which saves replies with wp_insert_comment() and bypasses the kses filtering WordPress normally applies to comment content. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page, by submitting a comment that leads the AI model to reproduce an HTML payload in its automated reply. This is only exploitable when an administrator has configured a Comment Auto-Reply automation task with 'Action on reply' set to 'Approve' (the default is 'Hold for moderation'), and the attacker's comment has been approved.

Zyrabit Platform provides sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 2.4.4, import_to_vault(source_path, destination_name) accepts both caller-controlled paths, but the content-pattern guard does not confine destination_name. The vulnerable tool is implemented in zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/domain/services/mcp_service.py, where Path(DOCS_DIR) / destination_name is passed to shutil.copy2, allowing traversal or an absolute destination to write outside the vault. An unrestricted source_path can be copied into the vault and retrieved through secure_query, disclosing files readable by the service; files that do not match the executable-pattern filter pass that filter. When ENABLE_LEGACY_EXTENSIONS=true, zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/main.py registers POST /mcp/rpc without get_current_user, allowing unauthenticated network tool calls; this optional exposure is disabled by default and is not required for local invocation. If an attacker can stage chosen source content and write to an execution-triggered destination, the advisory describes conditional process execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.4.

Bazarr is a companion application to Sonarr and Radarr. Prior to 1.6.3-beta.11, the /api/subtitles/subtitles-info handler uses SubtitleNameContents.get() in subtitles_contents.py and reads the caller-supplied subtitlePath after checking only its subtitle extension; because the resolved path is not confined to files indexed by Bazarr, traversal can read files outside the media library. The /api/subtitles/subtitles handler in subtitles.py passes caller-supplied path and reference to sync and translation without per-path authorization, allowing an out-of-library reference file to be read and output to overwrite a file outside the media library. The authenticate decorator gates both endpoints when API authentication is enabled, while auth = None allows access without credentials. Both paths can affect only files that the Bazarr process can read or write. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.3-beta.11.

The SNORDIAN's H5PxAPIkatchu plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'xapi' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.4.24 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the unauthenticated insert endpoint is publicly exposed in the listener.js script URL on every page displaying H5P content, making the injection trivially exploitable by any anonymous visitor.

In Eclipse versions 1.5-1.6.13, 2.0.0-2.0.22 and 2.1.0-2.1.2, the client library libmosquitto does not reject Will messages with payloads greater than 65535 bytes when calling `mosquitto_will_set()` or `mosquitto_will_set_v5()`. This results in up to 65535 bytes of uninitialised heap memory being transmitted as the Will.



This can be mitigated by only passing payloads with a maximum length of 65535 bytes.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Cozmoslabs Paid Member Subscriptions paid-member-subscriptions allows Code Injection.This issue affects Paid Member Subscriptions: from n/a through 3.1.4.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Cozmoslabs TranslatePress translatepress-multilingual allows Stored XSS.This issue affects TranslatePress: from n/a through 3.3.9.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in BdThemes Element Pack Elementor Addons bdthemes-element-pack-lite allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects Element Pack Elementor Addons: from n/a through 10.0.9.

A time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils (amazon-efs-utils) before 3.3.5 might allow a user that can start EFS mounts on a shared host to read and write a different Amazon EFS or S3 Files file system that is mounted on that same host, under that mount's IAM identity and access point, via concurrent mount operations. Only file systems mounted on the same host at the same time can be affected. Every mount involved was configured by the owner of that host, using credentials and access points that owner controls, against file systems whose owners had already granted that host access, so the issue grants no access beyond what the host was already permitted and does not cross AWS account boundaries unless the host's owner configured a cross-account mount. The practical risk is lateral access between workloads on the same host at the same time, for example one container reading another container's file system under that container's identity. The issue does not expose the other mount's IAM credentials or TLS session keys.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade amazon-efs-utils to version 3.3.5 or later. Users of the Amazon EFS CSI Driver should upgrade to version 3.5.4 or later, and users of the Amazon EKS EFS CSI add-on should update to v3.5.4-eksbuild.1 or later.

Incorrect authorization in the credential loading logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by another namespace's AWS Private CA with that namespace's stored AWS credentials, via a namespace-scoped issuer that references a credentials Secret in that namespace.



To remediate this issue, users should first copy any credentials Secret they intend a namespace-scoped issuer to use into that issuer's namespace and update the issuer's secretRef.namespace to match. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, from every AWS Private CA and certificate template reachable by the controller's own AWS identity or by any IAM role that identity can assume. This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity.



To remediate this issue, users should first update any namespace-scoped issuers that rely on the controller's identity to use their own credentials. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

Relative path traversal in the object detection dataset preparation tool in AutoGluon Multimodal before 1.6.0 might allow adversary-in-the-middle attackers to write arbitrary files with the privileges of the user running the tool via a crafted dataset archive substituted for a dataset downloaded over plaintext HTTP.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade autogluon.multimodal to version 1.6.0 or later.

A path traversal flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with ansible-galaxy collection install, the install destination directory is derived from the namespace and name fields declared inside the collection artifact's own metadata, which are not validated as well-formed collection identifiers or checked for path containment. A malicious collection artifact -- delivered as a local file, a remote URL, a source directory, a git repository, or as a dependency -- can use a crafted name value to redirect the install destination outside the configured collections path, causing ansible-galaxy to delete an existing directory writable by the invoking user and then write attacker-controlled files to that location.

WWBN AVideo from 6.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload permission to inject script by submitting a javascript: scheme videoLink for embed videos. The unvalidated URL is rendered into an iframe src in videoEmbeded.php and PlayerSkins.php, executing for viewers including administrators and enabling creation of new administrator accounts.

WWBN AVideo from 11.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with streaming permission to inject HTML by supplying an unvalidated url parameter to plugin/LiveLinks/play.php. Attackers can embed a --> sequence to escape the HTML comment in liveVideo.php, creating a shareable link that executes JavaScript in any visitor's session.

WWBN AVideo through c3edcc274c389816d434acadac07ee78eaf330c1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability because the default node socket server relays autoEvalCodeOnHTML without the PHP-only filter. Unauthenticated attackers can obtain an anonymous socket token and send a spoofed MSG_BATCH message to trigger client eval() in administrators' browsers for account takeover.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a stack overflow vulnerability in the MSVG decoder that allows attackers to crash the application by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit a malicious image for processing to exhaust the stack and terminate the application, causing denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated heap memory by triggering the -copy operation. Attackers can supply crafted images or arguments processed with -copy to crash the application or disclose adjacent heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to read from disallowed paths due to a missing policy check when decoding MPC files. Attackers can supply crafted MPC files that reference restricted locations to access files the configured security policy should block.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a data tampering vulnerability in the Distributed Pixel Cache that allows adjacent attackers to modify pixel data in transit between client and server. Attackers who can observe or modify the network path between a configured DPC client and server can tamper with pixel data to alter the resulting image.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the BGR, CMYK, GRAY, RGB, YCBCR and YUV decoders that allows attackers to crash the application. Attackers can supply a crafted image to these decoders to trigger a crash and disrupt image processing services.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MNG decoder that allows attackers to expose uninitialized memory by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit malicious MNG files for processing to leak uninitialized memory contents, potentially revealing sensitive data from the process.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability on Windows that allows attackers to evade path-based security policies by mixing forward slash and backslash separators. Attackers can supply crafted image file paths using alternate separators to read or write image files that the configured policy is intended to block.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the RLA decoder that returns images containing uninitialized data. Attackers can supply a crafted RLA image to cause the decoded output to include uninitialized memory, potentially disclosing heap information.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in various coders that allows attackers to allocate excessive memory by supplying images with many profiles. Attackers can craft images containing a high number of embedded profiles to exhaust memory and cause denial of service, bypassing security policy limits.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the MVG decoder that allows attackers to read out-of-bounds memory by supplying a crafted file. Attackers can provide a malicious MVG file for processing to trigger the over-read, causing application crashes or exposure of heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in the ASE decoder caused by a missing security policy check. Attackers can supply crafted ASE files that evade configured resource policies to cause excessive memory usage and denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the MSL decoder that can be triggered when processing crafted MSL image files. Attackers can supply a specially crafted MSL image to cause memory corruption, potentially crashing the application or leading to further compromise.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a code injection vulnerability in the MAGICK, XBM, XPM and UIL encoders that allows local attackers to inject content via crafted filenames. Attackers with access to the output directory and control over the filename can inject additional headers or code into the generated image source output.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability that allows attackers to write beyond allocated heap memory by supplying crafted images. Attackers can provide a crafted set of images processed by the magick stream operation to corrupt heap memory and crash the application.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the EXR decoder that is triggered when a specific memory allocation fails. Attackers can supply crafted EXR images processed under memory pressure to trigger the use after free, causing crashes or memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to evade resource limits because a policy check is missing when reading XMP profiles. Attackers can supply an image with a crafted XMP profile to trigger excessive memory usage and cause denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the TIFF decoder that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted TIFF image. Attackers can provide a malicious TIFF file that, when encoded in a specific output format, triggers a heap buffer over-write causing memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a double free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger an invalid memory free by using the DPC compare metric. Attackers can supply images for comparison with the DPC metric to corrupt memory and crash the application, causing denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the process by using the -subimage option on a single-image list. Attackers can supply input producing an image list with only one image while -subimage is applied, causing a denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated memory when BGRO image data is imported. Attackers can supply crafted BGRO data for processing to crash the application or leak adjacent heap memory contents.

Parse Server before 8.6.119 and 9.x before 9.10.8-alpha.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows LiveQuery clients without the master key to subscribe to installation and internal classes. Attackers can receive installation IDs and device tokens of other devices when these classes are in liveQuery.classNames, then modify those installations to redirect push notifications.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ChartsController::actionGetNewUsersData() that lacks a viewUsers permission check. Authenticated control panel users can POST to the charts/get-new-users-data action to read aggregate user-registration time series and totals for the site or any user group.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.5 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to inject raw SQL by passing nested array parameters into Element::findOne() criteria. Attackers can set the query's where property through endpoints like users/delete-address and users/save-address to perform blind boolean or time-based injection and read database contents.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains an incomplete blocklist fix that allows attackers who can author entry type title formats to write arbitrary files using ZipArchive or XMLWriter classes. Attackers can abuse the non-sandboxed renderObjectTemplate() renderer to write attacker-controlled content into the web docroot, achieving remote code execution.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in ImageTransforms::normalizeTransform() that allows attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes by supplying class:null with a __class key. Attackers can reach the method through Craft Commerce's payments/pay redirect template calling customer.photo.getUrl() with a crafted transform to instantiate classes like yii\rbac\PhpManager and execute PHP.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege control panel users to inject JavaScript by poisoning cached license data. Attackers can store a malicious licensed domain via the app/process-api-response-headers endpoint, which executes unescaped in administrators' dashboard license-mismatch warnings.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains an improper session management vulnerability that fails to invalidate existing sessions when 2FA is enabled and allows disabling 2FA without re-authentication. Attackers holding a hijacked or stale session can retain full account access and silently remove 2FA without the password, authenticator code, or recovery code.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to execute script by storing malicious Attribute View column names rendered unescaped in col.ts. Attackers can inject HTML via addAttributeViewKey, .sy.zip import, or sync, and when a victim adds or duplicates the column, insertAdjacentHTML runs JavaScript with Node.js privileges for desktop code execution.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in genAVValueHTML() that allows attackers who can store Attribute View asset values to inject script through an unescaped image src attribute. Attackers can store an image URL containing a double quote and onerror handler that executes OS commands via Node.js in the desktop app when victims open the bound note or row attribute panel.

SiYuan from 3.3.0 before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject HTML via unescaped checkbox column names in Gallery and Kanban AttributeView renderers. Attackers can share a crafted .sy.zip document whose rendering in the Electron desktop client with nodeIntegration enabled executes Node.js and host OS commands.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-44670, because renderAVAttribute() inserts an Attribute View name unescaped into the database row attribute panel header. Attackers who can persist the name, such as via the setAttrViewName action, can inject an onerror handler that runs OS commands through Node.js when a desktop user opens the panel.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 persists a table block's caption attribute into IAL properties without HTML sanitization, causing stored cross-site scripting upon import or sync. Attackers can inject an entity-encoded caption with an onerror handler that executes in the Electron client's nodeIntegration context to achieve remote code execution.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 uses an incomplete deny-list in IsSensitivePath that omits shell-initialization files such as .zshenv and .bash_profile, as well as ~/.local. Authenticated administrators can call /api/file/copyFile with an absolute destination outside the workspace to write payloads there, which execute as the user on the next shell or login.

vLLM before 0.33.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious model publishers to redirect the served model and tokenizer by setting speculators_config verifier.name_or_path in config.json. Attackers can point this field at another local checkpoint directory to leak its tokenizer vocabulary via unauthenticated /detokenize requests and gain query access to private models.

vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.

vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree during table creation. Attackers can set a malicious binary-expression operator that is interpolated into a knex.raw fragment, reading user and token tables and escalating to super administrator on SQLite installs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows organization Creators to reach routes restricted to other roles because the aclFn middleware never enforced allowedRoles. Attackers can generate a super admin password reset link via org-users endpoints to take over the instance, or read and modify SSO client secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form property paths to Handlebars helpers in webhook templates. Attackers can bypass the string-only prototype guard to reach the function constructor, running operating-system commands with server privileges or exfiltrating process-internal values via outbound requests.

NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the DATETIME_FORMAT formula format argument on MySQL-backed bases. Attackers can place a backslash before a quote to terminate the DATE_FORMAT string literal and read any data reachable by the data source's database user, including tables outside the base.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting them through the session header. Attackers can bypass revocation, client-existence, route allowlist and granted_resources scope checks to modify victim profiles, upload to storage, and force global sign-outs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a consent phishing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register OAuth clients with arbitrary HTTPS redirect URIs through the unauthenticated dynamic client registration endpoint. Attackers can impersonate trusted applications on a consent screen lacking unverified-client warnings or redirect host display, obtaining tokens to read and write victim tables and records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations. Attackers can trigger baseUserInviteResend to mint a new invite_token, read it from the base member list, and reset the victim's password through signup, taking over owner or super admin accounts.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column lists. Attackers with a shared view link can pair a visible and hidden column to bypass restrictSharedViewColumnReferences and retrieve hidden values tied to individual rows.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows Creator-role users to attach NocoDB's internal database by supplying is_meta and is_local flags. Attackers can create sources or bases with these flags to expose user, token and integration tables, then read and modify records including user roles.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared view link holders to read hidden columns by grouping on physical column names. Attackers can supply a hidden column's physical name or the unchecked sub-group parameter to the public group-by endpoint to reveal hidden values, counts, and column existence.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree reused without revalidation. Attackers can bypass the SQLite metadata path guard with an alias to plant the tree, escalating to super administrator or executing OS commands on external PostgreSQL hosts.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook plugin listing endpoint. Attackers can replay exposed Slack, Teams, Discord and Mattermost webhook URLs directly against messaging providers to post arbitrary messages into organization chat channels.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars webhook helpers. Attackers can supply property paths like constructor.constructor to pluck, sortBy, filter, or withSort helpers to reach the Function constructor and run operating-system commands.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator. Unauthenticated attackers with a job id can read buffered status messages and completion payloads, exposing signed export download URLs or new base identifiers.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated Creators to access another tenant's external database by reusing a victim source id when adding a source. Because NcConnectionMgrv2 caches connections by bare source id, attackers can reflect the victim's cached database schema and read, update, and insert records through their own base models.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up endpoint responses. Attackers can submit addresses to signup in users.service.ts and compare error messages to identify existing accounts and pending Enterprise invitations, even under invite-only signup.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid. Attackers holding an unexpired reset link, such as from prior mailbox access, can set a new password and regain control of the account.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because the read-by-primary-key path ignores the view's filters. Attackers can request the public attachment-download or nested-link listing routes with a record id to mint signed download URLs for hidden files and read linked-record data.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through the general base metadata endpoint. Attackers with a share link can query the base read or list responses in bases.controller.ts, which skip password stripping in sanitizeBase.ts, to obtain reusable plaintext passwords.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access records hidden by a shared view's row filter by supplying arbitrary primary keys. Attackers with the share link can request attachment downloads and many-to-many or has-many link listings for excluded records to obtain their attachment files and linked record identities.

NocoDB from 2026.06.2 before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to write to data-read-only sources by abusing the internal batch endpoint. Attackers can name a writable decoy table on the batch envelope and target a read-only source table in dataUpdate, dataInsert or dataDelete sub-operations to modify or destroy records.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in shared-view relation endpoints because parent-record lookups apply only the primary key, not the view's row filter. Anonymous share-link holders can enumerate auto-increment primary keys against the has-many, many-to-many, one-to-many and link-to-another-record routes to read linked records of filtered-out rows.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared view attachment-download endpoint. Attackers holding a public share link can enumerate sequential primary keys to obtain signed download paths for files on records the view's row filter excludes.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to the integration remote fetch operation. Attackers can control the method, headers, and body to reach internal APIs, loopback services, and cloud metadata endpoints, reading responses and echoed decrypted integration secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by storing foreign attachment paths in their own rows via prepareNocoData. Attackers with write access to an attachment column can have _convertAttachmentType or the attachment download endpoint sign the foreign path, reading cross-base files despite secure attachment mode.

NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements without numeric validation. Authenticated users with the Creator or Owner base role can supply a crafted precision value when creating or updating a column to close the type declaration and execute arbitrary SQL against the base's data source.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to register OAuth clients with javascript: redirect URIs. Attackers can send a consent link to a signed-in victim so either consent button runs script in the NocoDB origin, stealing the session token for account takeover.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's row filters. Unauthenticated attackers holding a public share link can supply guessable auto-incrementing ids of filtered-out records to has-many, many-to-many, one-many, or link endpoints to read their child records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the instance JWT secret. Attackers can present a narrowly scoped OAuth token to the session strategy, short-lived-token exchange, or NocoSocket handshake to gain the granting user's full privileges.

NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

Traefik from 2.11.58 before 2.11.61 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust resources by sending Authorization headers with NTLM or Negotiate schemes. Attackers can open many short-lived connections that each allocate a dedicated backend transport never released, exhausting memory, file descriptors and backend connections.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage key delimiter collisions and PageStorage folder reconstruction. Attackers can rename a folder like locked*** or save from a page with an unusual prefix width through a front-end Flex pages form, replacing protected content and permissions to access the protected subtree.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer. Attackers can upload SVG files with inner extensions like .svg.defaults, payloads that crash the fail-open sanitizer, or unblocked .xml/.xhtm files to run script when administrators open the raw file URL.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image titles, alt text, class, id, or file names. Attackers can combine injected Twig with the autoescape tag to serve script to every page visitor, including super admins, or expose unpublished page content.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers to bypass the media action allowlist using scoped method names in Markdown image URLs. Attackers can chain actions like self::addMetaFile into static calls such as Process::fromShellCommandline to read files and run shell commands as the web server user.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers to grant super-admin rights by nesting access maps under a YAML merge key. Attackers with admin.users.create or api.users.write can submit '<<' keys, for example via PATCH /api/v1/users/<self>, that bypass super-grant filtering and gain full site control.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers with admin.users.update to take over super admin accounts by disabling the super-granting group. Attackers can set the group's enabled field to false via the Flex user-groups form, then reset the victim's password through the user-accounts form to gain super admin access.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers and Flex editors to overwrite, create, or delete accounts by supplying client-controlled storage keys. Attackers can abuse the create form username, cross-type form flash replay, or __META storage key rename to gain super-admin accounts or delete account files.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows publishers and read-only user managers to read password hashes, 2FA secrets and reset tokens through unfiltered account serialization. Attackers can embed a Flex form for the user-accounts directory in a page or query the Flex API with admin.users.read to obtain super admin credentials and take over the account.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig sandbox bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to read any server file by abusing allowlisted array_key_value() and page accessor setters such as filePath(). Attackers can repoint page objects or overwrite the assets collections to render private keys and the API signing secret, then forge a super-admin API token.

Grav 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 resolves Flex sort and filter field names by first calling them as public methods, so a field named delete invokes FlexObject::delete() without any permission check. Authenticated users with only list access can send GET /api/v1/flex-objects/user-accounts?sort=delete requests to delete every account, then use the reopened API first-run setup to create a super admin.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows page editors to escape the Twig sandbox by sending requests with a Host: pages header. Attackers can write configuration YAML through page folders and media .meta.yaml sidecars to register an unsandboxed Twig namespace and run shell commands as the web server user.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page cache key. Routine editor activity through the API plugin rebuilds the page index without frontmatter.yaml access rules, exposing members-only page content until the cache is rebuilt.

Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 serves page media files, and rendered pages when lazy sessions are enabled, with the visitor's session cookie and a shared-cacheable Cache-Control header. When a shared cache such as Apache mod_cache stores Set-Cookie responses, an attacker can lure a user signed in through the front-end login to open a media URL with a unique query string, then request that URL to receive the cached session cookie and take over the session.

Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to create super-admin accounts because UserCollection::count() uses an unescaped glob() pattern. On installs whose path contains brackets or a backslash, the account count returns zero, so attackers can send requests to POST /api/v1/auth/setup or the classic admin registration form to create or overwrite administrator accounts.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to redirect reset links by forging the CloudFront-Forwarded-Proto header. Attackers can send a forgot-password request with a crafted scheme value so the emailed reset link points to their host, capturing the token to take over accounts including super admins.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to fill the disk by varying the HTTP Host header. Attackers can send requests with distinct Host values to create per-host compiled configuration, blueprint, language and page index caches, causing session, upload and logging failures.

Network-AI from 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 contains a CORS misconfiguration in McpStreamableServer that reflects localhost Origins into Access-Control-Allow-Origin regardless of bind interface. Attackers controlling a localhost-origin page or DNS-rebinding name can read unauthenticated /tools and /health responses, exposing tool catalogs and bridge metadata on non-loopback binds.

OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-travelmate on master before 3.0.0-1 and on openwrt-25.12 before 2.4.9-6 grants file exec permissions for state-mutating commands in the read scope of its rpcd ACL, letting authenticated read-only users run those commands as root. Attackers can invoke ubus file exec on /etc/init.d/travelmate setup, start, stop, restart, or /sbin/ifup to modify and commit network and firewall configuration or disrupt the travelmate daemon.

OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-uhttpd before commit d38658bedbdd811b798da16b49301478c6cf21af grants '/*' file read in its rpcd read ACL, which rpcd's fnmatch matching applies to every path. Users delegated only luci-app-uhttpd read access can read any file as root, including /etc/shadow, /etc/config/* credentials, /etc/uhttpd.key, and /etc/dropbear keys.

heym before 0.0.142 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Playwright step-mode node where _resolve_expressions_in_code substitutes workflow values directly into generated Python source. Authenticated non-admin users can craft step field values that break out of string literals to execute arbitrary Python as root inside the backend container.

All versions of LaraDashboard contain an authentication bypass in SocialAuthService::findOrCreateUser(), which links a social login to an existing account by email without checking that the OAuth provider verified that email. Unauthenticated attackers using an OAuth/OIDC provider that asserts a victim's email can log in as any user, including Superadmin, and keep persistent access through a linked social_accounts entry.

Froxlor before 2.3.16 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to read hidden traffic statistics by calling the Traffic.listing API command. Attackers can authenticate to api.php with their API key and secret to retrieve HTTP, FTP, and mail traffic volumes despite the panel.customer_hide_options restriction.

pnpm exe before 10.34.8 embeds an outdated Node.js runtime that still trusts compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates during registry TLS connections. Network attackers holding a recovered intermediate key can intercept standalone pnpm registry fetches and serve forged package metadata or tarballs.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse case-mutated security tokens because MySQL token columns used case-insensitive collation. Attackers holding a case-normalized invite or email-change token can redirect a victim's email for account takeover or redeem invites with roles up to Global Admin.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the deprecated POST /api/latest/fleet/mdm/apple/enqueue endpoint that allows team-scoped users to enqueue Apple MDM commands outside their teams. Attackers with team admin, maintainer, or GitOps roles can include one own-team host UUID alongside unresolved enrollment IDs to send commands like InstallProfile to deleted or user-channel enrollments without activity logging.

Fleet from 4.71.0 before 4.88.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SAML SSO callback that looks up sessions using unvalidated client-supplied identifiers. Users able to run live queries or enroll secret holders can plant attacker-controlled identity provider metadata in the session store, then present a self-signed SAML response to log in as a global admin.

Fleet before 4.86.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via unbounded BER recursion in PKCS#7 parsing. Attackers can send deeply nested indefinite-length structures to Apple MDM check-in, enrollment, SCEP, or OTA endpoints to crash the entire Fleet instance.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows enrolled hosts to trigger unbounded per-name database lookups by submitting osquery result logs. Attackers with a valid host node key can send one request to /api/osquery/log containing many distinct query names, exhausting database connections and read replica capacity.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated observer-level users to sort software listings by arbitrary columns via the order_key parameter. Attackers can order by joined hosts table columns such as node keys and use pagination as a binary-search oracle to extract sensitive column values.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in the host inventory export endpoint that allows attackers controlling an enrolled host or enroll secret to plant spreadsheet formulas. Attackers can set osquery-reported fields like hostname or hardware serial to formula values, enabling data exfiltration or DDE command execution when users open the exported CSV.

Obot from 0.8.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power User accounts to reach internal hosts by advertising a malicious OAuth token endpoint in remote MCP server metadata. Attackers can direct token exchange or refresh requests, including redirected GET requests, to cloud metadata services or private-network hosts and read error response bodies.

Obot before 0.27.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass same-site validation of the rd parameter by inserting a tab character. Attackers can craft sign-in or sign-out links on the Obot domain that browsers resolve to external hosts, redirecting victims to phishing pages.

Obot from 0.26.0 before 0.27.0 fails to validate the resource identifier in remote MCP server protected resource metadata, allowing malicious MCP servers to steal access tokens. Attackers can name a different service and authorization server with chosen scopes, causing Obot to obtain the victim's token for that service and forward it to the attacker.

Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.

Obot from 0.14.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power Users to bypass outbound protections by supplying unspecified addresses, IPv6 transition addresses, or registry icon URLs. Attackers can add remote MCP servers pointing to 0.0.0.0, ::, or NAT64/6to4/Teredo addresses embedding blocked IPv4 addresses to probe internal services for reachability.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows clients permitted to create instances to crash the daemon by importing a backup with a null snapshot entry in index.yaml. Attackers can trigger an unrecovered nil pointer dereference during configuration rewrite, terminating the daemon and all containers and virtual machines on the node.

Incus before 7.6.0 creates the NBD servers used for virtual machine migration and disk export on abstract unix sockets, which have no permission checks and whose names are visible in /proc/net/unix. A local unprivileged user can connect while an operation runs to read or modify the VM disk, gaining code execution in the guest on a migration's receiving side.

Incus before 7.6.0 fails to reject special files, hard links, or symlinks in backup or image metadata, allowing restricted project users to read or overwrite host files. Attackers can import crafted backups containing device nodes, a hard-linked backup.yaml, or symlinks to corrupt host storage, overwrite host files, or leak other projects' data.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted TLS clients to read other projects' bucket S3 keys and profile configuration through recursive and all-projects responses. Attackers can query bucket listings with recursion=2 or profiles with all-projects=true to obtain S3 secret keys and sensitive environment, cloud-init and user values across projects.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows restricted project users to create resources in the unrestricted default project by targeting projects lacking features.* flags. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq dhcp-script injection to run scripts as root, or custom volumes with block.create_options mkfs arguments to read host files.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability: rebuilding a never-started unprivileged container makes it boot without a user namespace. Root processes inside the container run as host uid 0, keeping capabilities like sys_module, with no device cgroup restriction, letting them load kernel modules and compromise the host.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest-API image export handler that fails to pin the project parameter to the guest's own project. Container root users with the guest-API image entitlement can supply another project in the project query parameter to export public or cached images, including non-public images pulled from authenticated remotes.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients with project event-view access to read migration websocket secrets broadcast in operation metadata. Attackers can connect to in-flight migration control and fs websockets before the legitimate peer, hijacking the transfer to obtain instance configuration and filesystem data.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project-restricted authenticated clients to receive other projects' OVN ACL logs because these events are broadcast with an empty project. Attackers can subscribe to network-acl events on one accessible project to observe internal IPs, ports, protocols, and allow/drop decisions across all projects.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to authenticate as any trusted certificate by appending its public certificate to their presented TLS client chain. Attackers can append the server's or a cluster member's certificate to gain cluster-level access, bypass authorization, modify trust store entries, and influence scriptlet-based authorization decisions.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users permitted to import custom volumes to store unvalidated snapshot names from the backup index configuration section. Attackers can craft a backup with traversal sequences in snapshot names so later deletion removes arbitrary host directories as root, while renaming or mounting operates on arbitrary paths.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious migration peers to write outside intended directories by supplying unvalidated dependent volume and snapshot names in the migration offer header. Attackers controlling a migration source can create root-owned volumes with attacker content at arbitrary host paths, compromising hosts using dir storage pools, bypassing restricted.storage-pools.access, or crashing the daemon.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the storage bucket S3 listener, which buffers entire signed request bodies in memory before verifying the signature or credential role. Attackers knowing only a valid access key, or holding a read-only credential, can send many concurrent large requests to exhaust daemon memory.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted and view-only clients to read default project resources by requesting the default project directly. Attackers knowing resource names can read profiles, images, network zone peer keys and stored credentials, and export custom volume or bucket backups to obtain full contents or S3 admin keys.

Incus before 7.6.0 exposes certificate and cluster join token secrets through the default project event stream and skips authorization when cancelling operations without associated permissions. Restricted clients can subscribe to operation events to capture certificate tokens and enroll unrestricted certificates, gaining full server access, or cancel token operations by UUID.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted clients to create and access default project resources by exploiting entitlement checks against the requested project. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq directives to execute code as root on the host, or manipulate inherited resources via the ?project= parameter.

Incus from 7.3.0 before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest API that allows a process in one container to impersonate another by creating a cgroup named with a forged lxc.monitor. component. Attackers can read the target container's user.* and cloud-init.* configuration and devices, subscribe to its events, mark it ready, and export images across projects.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows users who can launch instances from controlled images to inject LXC directives by embedding line breaks in OCI config.json values or oci.entrypoint and oci.cwd keys. Attackers can add liblxc hooks or crafted tmpfs lxc.mount.entry fields to run commands as root on the host or bind-mount host paths, even from restricted projects.

Frappe ERPNext before 16.35.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in financial reporting endpoints that allows low-privilege authenticated users to generate reports outside their permitted scope. Attackers can send crafted requests to affected reporting endpoints to read other companies' tax and payment data, including personal and corporate identifiers and financial totals.

SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in CsvFileExportPrinter and DsvResultPrinter via unescaped valuesep and separator parameters. Attackers can craft Special:Ask links using request_type=special_page so export output renders as text/html, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers under the wiki origin.

SemanticMediaWiki from 7.3.0 before 7.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the smwtask API check-query task that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass object-level authorization by relying on the wiki-wide edit right. Attackers can supply arbitrary subject titles, including protected pages, to run synchronous Semantic MediaWiki queries with caller-controlled conditions, limit, offset, and querymode parameters.

SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup reference names in MediaWiki:Smw_allows_pattern. Once an editor annotates the matching Allows pattern value, AllowsPatternValue emits it unescaped on Special:Browse, executing JavaScript in every viewer's session.

Finsys Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows users with stacks:edit permission to move arbitrary server directories by supplying a crafted oldDir parameter. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/stacks/[name]/relocate with an unvalidated source path to relocate directories into stack paths, disrupting services and exposing their contents.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow in gf_xml_sax_parse_intern() in src/utils/xml_parser.c that causes a heap-based buffer overflow when completing partially buffered entities. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XML or XMT file with MP4Box, overflowing xml_sax_append_string() size arithmetic to corrupt heap memory and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in gf_filter_pid_resolve_file_template_ex() in src/filter_core/filter_pid.c that allows local attackers to write past fixed GF_MAX_PATH stack buffers. Attackers can convince a user to segment a crafted NHML input referencing an overly long media file name with MP4Box -dash to crash the process.

Frappe HR (hrms) before 16.9.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the hrms.api.roster.get_events method that allows authenticated employees to view other employees' leave and shift data by bypassing User Permissions. Attackers with the Employee role can call get_events with empty filters for any date range to retrieve every employee's approved leave applications and shift assignments, including leave types, dates, shift locations and times.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying unbalanced command buffer closing elements. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT-A file with MP4Box, causing xmt_node_end() to treat a GF_Command as an SFCommandBuffer and crash the process.

Flowise 3.1.3 through 3.1.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read MCP server bearer tokens via the GET /api/v1/public-chatflows/:id handler. Attackers can use the leaked mcpServerConfig token on the POST /api/v1/mcp/:chatflowId route to invoke chatflows, bypassing API key protection and consuming the owner's model quota.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a use of uninitialized variable vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying duplicate PROTO field names. Attackers can trick a user into opening a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_parse_sf_field() to write through an uninitialized pointer and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that leaves dangling MFURL pointers when xmt_node_end() discards nodes. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to access freed heap memory and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that frees a node when a DEF attribute names a previously referenced undefined node. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing freed heap memory to be used and crashing the process.

The device's command parser does not require asymmetric cryptographic signatures to validate incoming APDU packets. This enables an attacker to inject forged, unauthorized commands to manipulate device features and configurations once the initial handshake is bypassed.

The NFC authentication handshake relies on a fixed, static challenge instead of a unique, random value for every session. This allows an attacker to perform a "replay attack," successfully authenticating by simply sending the same pre-recorded response.

The firmware and flash memory store critical cryptographic secrets, such as global AES keys and network master keys, in unencrypted formats. Additionally, active session tokens (Store Pairing Tokens) are written to the flash in plaintext, exposing live network credentials.

The microcontroller lacks enabled debug lock bits, leaving the physical Single-Wire (SWS) debugging interface completely unrestricted. This allows an attacker with physical access to use a hardware programmer to dump the entire production firmware.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Igor Funa Ad Inserter ad-inserter allows Code Injection.This issue affects Ad Inserter: from n/a through 2.8.19.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_new_od_link_from_node() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file with an MFURL object-descriptor link lacking an OD ID and name, crashing MP4Box for denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in load_xmt_done() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that releases references for duplicate node stack entries. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file encoded with MP4Box to crash the process and potentially corrupt heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying XMT-A elements that define and use the same node identifier. Attackers can craft an XMT scene file processed by MP4Box so xmt_text_content() accesses the freed node, crashing the process and possibly corrupting heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process via ROUTE elements. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file placing a ROUTE element before any scene command creates an access unit, crashing MP4Box during encoding and causing denial of service.

Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b contains an integer underflow in plm_demux_seek() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via crafted MPEG-PS files. Attackers can supply a PES packet with payload under 6 bytes, wrapping the packet->length - 6 loop bound during force_intra seeking to crash applications.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to access freed memory via a dangling command buffer pointer. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file whose Replace command frees a Conditional node, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting the heap.

Storyden before 1.26.17 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the AccountRemoveRole handler that allows non-administrator users with MANAGE_ROLES to remove administrator roles. Attackers can send DELETE requests to the account roles endpoint to demote other administrators, potentially leaving the instance with no administrator.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an invalid pointer free vulnerability in gf_sg_command_del() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that allows attackers to corrupt the heap via crafted XMT scene files. Attackers can supply an XMT-A file whose command field_ptr references the embedded new_node member, causing free() on an interior address and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in xmt_parse_mf_field() in loader_xmt.c caused by unchecked cursor advancement when splitting multi-value XMT-A fields. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file opened with MP4Box to make xmt_parse_string() read past the heap buffer and crash the process.

Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inherit group-based rights by reusing group memberships never reset between requests. Attackers can send credential-less requests after a group member logs in to read and write group-shared calendar and address book collections evaluated by the from_file rights backend.

ModelScope 1.11.0 to before 1.40.1 contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability in the image-to-3D SyncDreamer pipeline that allows remote attackers to execute code via crafted model configuration. Attackers can publish a model whose syncdreamer.yaml target field makes instantiate_from_config() import and instantiate any class with controlled params, without an allowlist or trust_remote_code check, executing code when victims load it.

BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to impersonate administrators by abusing a hard-coded default jwt_secret used by AuthJwt. Attackers can forge an HS256 token offline naming user_id 1 with the admin role, send it as access_token_cookie, and gain full administrative access to users, workspaces, knowledge bases and workflows.

ioBroker.lovelace before 7.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the onCards() request handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files via unsanitized dot-dot segments. Attackers can send crafted requests to the /cards/_static_/, /hacsfiles/, or /local/custom_ui/ routes to read files including ioBroker configuration and stored credentials.

HyperFrames before 0.8.73 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Studio server waveform and thumbnail routes that percent-decode paths without containment checks. Unauthenticated attackers, including script in a malicious composition, can send encoded ../ sequences to probe file existence and extract waveform data from files outside the project.

HyperFrames before 0.9.30 contains a missing Origin and Host validation vulnerability in the unauthenticated Studio API that allows malicious web pages to write project files. Attackers can send CORS-simple POST requests to /api/projects/:id/files/* or use DNS rebinding to plant package.json scripts or agent configs, leading to command execution.

HyperFrames before 0.8.216 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the engine URL downloader because isBlockedHost() only checks IP literals and never resolves DNS host names. Attackers can supply compositions with remote media, image or font URLs whose host names resolve to private addresses, making preview or render processes send HTTPS requests to internal services.

CodeIgniter4 before 4.7.5 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the View Parser (system/View/Parser.php) that allows attackers to bypass auto-escaping through re-scanned substitutions. Attackers controlling one rendered value can inject Parser syntax like {other|raw} or {!other!} to emit unescaped attacker-controlled values, executing scripts in viewers' browsers.

AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the TextareaAutosize component that allows workspace members with edit access to inject markup by copying unescaped values into a hidden mirror via innerHTML. Attackers can store a database row title or checklist task containing an element with an event handler to execute script in browsers of users opening the row, including unauthenticated published page visitors.

Dolibarr ERP CRM before 24.0.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the Users REST API put() method that allows non-admin API users to set administrator passwords. Authenticated users with user modification and password rights can send a PUT request to the users endpoint with a chosen pass value for a SuperAdmin account and then log in as that administrator.

Dolibarr ERP CRM through 24.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability in Website::importWebSite() that allows website editors without PHP permission to execute code by importing templates. Attackers can import a template zip whose javascript.js.php contains PHP code, which the public javascript.js.php endpoint includes, executing code as the web server user.

BZFlag bzfs before 2.4.32 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in NetHandler::tcpReceive() that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a TCP message with a body length of exactly 1024. Attackers can overwrite the tcplen receive offset with a negative value to write controlled bytes before the buffer, crashing the server or executing commands as the bzfs user.

LaraCollab through 0.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated client-role users to inject script by posting unsanitized task comments rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Attackers can post malicious comments that execute when users, including administrators, open the task or view dashboard recent comments, allowing actions in their session.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in User::ownsWishlist() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' wishes and wishlists. Attackers can supply sequential wish_id and wishlist_id values to the wishes and wishlists API handlers to edit wishes, add wishes, or rename and delete wishlists.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the PUT branch of src/api/wishes.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify wish URLs across all users. Attackers who know a wish link from a public wishlist can supply wish_url_current and wish_url_proposed parameters to redirect owners and gift-givers to attacker-controlled URLs.

Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users with permissions.manage to gain unauthorized permissions because addGroupMember and setUserGroups lack the grantsBeyondCaller check. Attackers can add their own account to custom groups via the group membership endpoints to inherit permissions like users.impersonate and settings.backup.

AudioBookRequest 1.9.0 through 2.0.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject script through manual book request fields due to disabled Jinja2 autoescaping. Attackers can submit malicious title, author, narrator or info values via POST /api/requests/manual to execute script in an administrator's browser and access admin-only endpoints.

Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.

53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to reinitialize installed instances by calling the public POST /api/init endpoint. Attackers can reset an existing account's password, assign the top creator role, and obtain an access token to take over accounts and use admin-only API routes.

EveryDocs Core before 1.6.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' records through unscoped Model.find(params[:id]) lookups in multiple controllers. Self-registered attackers can enumerate sequential ids to read, modify, or delete other users' documents and stored files, and rename or delete their folders, tags and people.

FS PBX through 2.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FaxesController, PaymentGatewayController and VirtualReceptionistController API routes that only check authentication. Any authenticated user can delete other tenants' fax records by UUID, deactivate or modify the platform-wide payment gateway, and change another tenant's IVR greeting.

Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.

Flagr before 1.2.5 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access the flag management write API through an insecure default FLAGR_BASIC_AUTH_WHITELIST_PATHS including /api/v1/flags. Because basicAuth.whitelist() in pkg/config/middleware.go matches only path prefixes regardless of HTTP method, attackers can create, modify, enable, disable, and delete flags, variants, segments, constraints, and distributions.

UrlHub before 1.20.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to create accounts via the POST /admin/user/store route because role:admin middleware only covers view and create actions. Attackers, including self-registered users, can submit a request with role=admin to create an administrator account and gain full administrative control.

BeikeShop through 2.0.0.32 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered customers to inject script by submitting an unsanitized RMA comment rendered unescaped in mail templates. Attackers can submit a return request with malicious script saved to mail_logs.content, executing in an administrator's browser session when they view the Mail Logs entry.

ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the IAM role management API that allows authenticated tenant members to escalate privileges. Attackers holding even the lowest built-in role can call the permissions/grant-ids, permissions/grant, or bind/member routes to grant permissions or bind privileged roles, gaining tenant administrative access.

Coyote before commit d6e8fb9 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Wiki\CommentController::save that allows authenticated users to edit other users' wiki comments. Attackers can send POST requests to /Comment/Save/{wiki}/{id} with another user's comment id, bypassing the WikiCommentPolicy update check, so altered text appears under the original author's name.

wireguard_webadmin before 0.9981 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in scheduler/views.py that allows low-privilege authenticated users to manage peer schedules without Peer Manager level. View Only or Debugging Analyst users can create, modify, and delete schedule profiles and time slots to disable WireGuard peers or keep disabled peers off.
